category_title: Difficult students who alternate between ostentatious task engagement and masked transgressive play
minimal_context: The student is waiting in line at the 'Jumping over' workshop in gymnastics class to practice straight jumps over the horse.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright everyone, we are at the 'Jumping over' workshop. Please line up and practice your straight jumps over the horse.

STUDENT: Teacher, look! I'm doing the exercise. Is it good? I need help for the stall turn so you can see I'm working!

TUTOR: Yes, that is fine. Keep practicing your jumps while I go check on the other group.

STUDENT: (Looks towards the teacher) There I make the jump, it's easy, I'm going to have fun. (Insults Aris as he prepares to jump over the horse, causing Aris to miss and fall).

TUTOR: What is going on over there? Please just do the straight jumps like I asked.

STUDENT: (Sees the teacher leaving) The teacher can't see us, he's looking in the other direction. Let's play at who will do the most spectacular jump! (Attempts a somersault instead of a straight jump).

options.A: Allow the students to have more of a say in the workshop activities and be a bit more liberal about how they execute the jumps.
options.B: Use body positioning to monitor the class, systematically associating learning rules with specific physical actions (gestures, spatial positions, or stares) to involve the students.
options.C: Implement relatively tight timelines for completing the straight jumps at the workshop, keeping the students on a strict schedule during the activity.
options.D: Provide a less frequent schedule of breaks intermittently throughout the gymnastics class, keeping the students at the workshop for longer continuous periods.
